commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

commit_message:
Fix arena allocation alignment at the block boundary (#24773)

This fixes an arena edge case where a request fits in a block before
alignment, but no longer fits after rounding. Such requests now use the
oversized allocation path, and oversized allocations keep their returned
pointers naturally aligned.

Added tests for both boundary cases.

Assisted by: Codex Sol

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

---------

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: Analyze (javascript)

commit_message:
[tools] Accept signed NPY expected outputs for signless integers

NumPy does not have a signless integer dtype, so writing an IREE signless integer buffer to NPY and reading it back changes its metadata to a signed integer. This caused expected-output comparison to fail before comparing the buffer contents.

Treat signed expected data as storage-compatible with same-width signless results during expected-output comparison. Integer contents remain compared exactly, and all other metadata mismatches are still rejected.

Add unit and iree-run-module regression tests.

Fixes #22080

## Testing

Locally passed:

- `iree/tooling/comparison_test`
- `iree/tooling/numpy_io_test`
- `iree/tools/test/iree-run-module-expected.mlir.test`

Manually verified that the reproducer from #22080 now reports that all function outputs match their expected values.

Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>

NumPy does not have a signless integer dtype, so writing an IREE signless integer buffer to NPY and reading it back changes its metadata to a signed integer. This caused expected-output comparison to fail before comparing the buffer contents.

Treat signed expected data as storage-compatible with same-width signless results during expected-output comparison. Integer contents remain compared exactly, and all other metadata mismatches are still rejected.

Add unit and iree-run-module regression tests.

Fixes #22080

## Testing

Locally passed:

- `iree/tooling/comparison_test`
- `iree/tooling/numpy_io_test`
- `iree/tools/test/iree-run-module-expected.mlir.test`

Manually verified that the reproducer from #22080 now reports that all function outputs match their expected values.

Co-authored-by: OpenAI <noreply@openai.com>
Signed-off-by: zhangpan <98025960+zhangpan2001@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

---------

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: linux_x64_gcc

correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Fix GatherFusionPattern on a scalar producer operand

GatherFusionPattern builds a tensor.extract for every operand of the
producer generic, so a scalar operand reached cast<TensorType> and
asserted. A scalar is invariant over the iteration space, so there is no
index to permute and nothing to extract: the fused body reads the value
itself.

The producer has to be a bit extend or a transpose to qualify, and that
classification deliberately ignores non-tensor inputs, so a qualifying
producer can have them. A per-tensor dequantize widening i8 to f32 with
its scale passed as an f32 is one.

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

---------

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: macos :: Build py-compiler-pkg Package

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

---------

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable unpack ops

Stacks on the scalable-pack hint support. Extend the alignment capture in
`MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs` to `linalg.unpack` ops:
after the loop tile sizes are scaled up into the unpacked (dest) domain by
`undoScaleAndPermutateTilingForUnpackOp`, each scalable inner tile is compared
against the (now scalable) loop tile on its dimension and the per-level result
is stashed as `iree_codegen.inner_tile_alignments`. This lets
`makeInnerTileAlignmentFn` read the unpack's alignment back instead of
recomputing it post-mortem. Distribution level excluded (see TODO).

commit_message:
feat(KernelDispatch): set inner-tile alignment hints on scalable pack ops

During tile-size selection, `MultiLoweringConfigGenerator::setNewTilingConfigs`
compares each scalable `linalg.pack` inner tile against the loop tile size chosen
for that dimension (`getScalableInnerTileAlignment`) and stamps the per-level
result via `InnerTileAlignmentsAttr::setOnOp`, before the loop tiles are
translated into the packed outer domain (`capturePackInnerTileAlignment`).

A `linalg.pack` whose producer is a `linalg.unpack` is pruned by
`shouldSetLoweringConfig` and never receives a lowering config, so it is not
visited by `setNewTilingConfigs`. Handle it separately in
`annotateScalablePackConsumerOfUnpack`: read the producer unpack's per-level tile
sizes and compare them against the pack's scalable inner tiles, stashing the same
`inner_tile_alignments` attribute.

The distribution level is intentionally skipped for now (see TODO).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
name: Analyze (actions)

commit_message:
[Codegen][LLVMCPU] Split loadProcessorData: hoist only the alloca (#24744)

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function entry
block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from the ukernel
call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer store-to-load forward the
forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime feature check across the
enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func select never devirtualizes and the
microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the actual
cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit patch at the call
site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no stack, so the stack stays
bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent to the (inlined) load and fold as
before, restoring devirtualization.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: pre-commit

35b2070 (#24749) fixed unbounded stack growth by moving the whole
loadProcessorData CPU-feature patch buffer construction to the function entry
block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from the ukernel
call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer store-to-load forward the
forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime feature check across the
enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func select never devirtualizes and the
microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the actual
cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit patch at the call
site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no stack, so the stack stays
bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent to the (inlined) load and fold as
before, restoring devirtualization.

Signed-off-by: Ege Beysel <beyselege@gmail.com>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_ops :: amdgpu_hip_rdna4_O3

block. But that also hoisted the feature-bit or/store away from the ukernel
call, and once the ukernel inlines, LLVM can no longer store-to-load forward the
forced feature bits into the ukernel's runtime feature check across the
enclosing loop, so the mmt4d/pack tile-func select never devirtualizes and the
microkernel is left out-of-line.

Split the two concerns: reserve only the alloca (the stack slot, the actual
cause of #24744) in the entry block, but keep the feature-bit patch at the call
site. The stores re-run per iteration but allocate no stack, so the stack stays
bounded while the forced bits remain adjacent to the (inlined) load and fold as
before, restoring devirtualization.

commit_message:
Fix arena allocation alignment at the block boundary (#24773)

This fixes an arena edge case where a request fits in a block before
alignment, but no longer fits after rounding. Such requests now use the
oversized allocation path, and oversized allocations keep their returned
pointers naturally aligned.

Added tests for both boundary cases.

Assisted by: Codex Sol

commit_message:
[LLVMCPU] Use native bf16 converts when the target supports them (#24759)

## Summary

The bf16 arithmetic is getting promoted to f32 in codegen, which is
correct for every CPU (there's no CPU with native bf16 arithmetic yet,
RISC-V `Zvfbfmin` provides conversions only). The conversions around
that promotion, however, are always expanded in software. That prevents
targets that do have bf16 <-> f32 conversion instructions from selecting
them, costing ~6 integer ops per narrow and 2 per widen on every bf16
load and store.

Introduce another LLVMCPULoweringPipeline option: it's set to true on
RISC-V targets with both `Zfbfmin` and `Zvfbfmin` extensions. Both are
required, since with only the vector extension scalar bf16 residue
lowers to `__truncsfbf2` libcalls. bf16 loads/stores and the promotion's
extf/truncf then select as `vfwcvtbf16/vfncvtbf16` (vector) and
`fcvt.s.bf16/fcvt.bf16.s` (scalar). This option is passed to
`ConvertUnsupportedFloatToIntBuffers` and `arith-expand` passes.

## Testing

Measured on a SpaceMiT K3 (X100 cores) (yay, i have access to one now).

Tested on kernels: 1M-element bf16 kernels, native vs current expansion,
outputs bit-identical in every case:

| kernel | native | expanded | speedup |
| :-- | --: | --: | --: |
| elementwise add | 0.800 ms | 1.45 ms | 1.81× |
| f32 to bf16 cast | 0.650 ms | 1.01 ms | 1.55× |
| sigmoid-weighted elementwise chain | 7.83 ms | 8.31 ms | 1.06× |
| bf16 to f32 cast | 0.494 ms | 0.538 ms | 1.09× |

Also tested on whole models: a bf16 `whisper-tiny-en` encoder-decoder
runs in **3.580 s vs 3.936 s (1.10×)** with bit-identical output against
PyTorch reference. A small CLIP-style bf16 model compiles to a 7.5%
smaller vmfb.

---------

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>
name: linux_x64_clang_byollvm
